''[[Nine (2009 live-action film)|Nine]]'' (10) | website = {{url|http://www.criticschoice.com}} | network = [[VH1]] | last = 14th | next = 16th }} The '''15th Critics' Choice Awards''' were presented on January 15, 2010 at the [[Hollywood Palladium]], honoring the finest achievements of [[2009 in film|2009 filmmaking]].{{cite mag |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/hurt-locker-tops-critics-choice-19589/ |title='Hurt Locker' tops Critics' Choice Awards |last1=Kit |first1=Borys |last2=Kilday |first2=Gregg |date=January 15, 2010 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=January 15, 2010}} The ceremony was broadcast on [[VH1]] and hosted by [[Kristin Chenoweth]].{{cite magazine article |url=https://ew.com/article/2009/12/09/kristin-chenoweth-to-host-critics-choice-movie-awards-gala/ |title=Kristin Chenoweth to host Critics' Choice Movie Awards gala |last=Ram |first=Archana |date=December 9, 2009 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=December 9, 2009}} The nominees were announced on December 14, 2009.{{cite Magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/basterds-nine-lead-critics-choice-92305/ |title='Basterds', 'Nine' lead Critics' Choice noms |last=Kilday |first=Gregg |date=December 14, 2009 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=December 14, 2009}} The awards expanded this year from 16 to 24 film categories, adding seven technical categories and separating its screenplay category into [[Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|adapted]] and [[Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Original Screenplay|original]] slots, to more closely mirror the [[Academy Awards]]. The [[World War II]] epic ''[[Inglourious Basterds]]'' and [[romance film|romantic]] [[musical film|musical drama]] ''[[Nine (2009 live-action film)|Nine]]'' both received a record ten nominations each,{{cite web |url=https://www.thewrap.com/inglourious-basterds-nine-lead-critics-choice-nominations-11729/ |title='Inglourious Basterds', 'Nine' lead Critics Choice Nominations |last=Pond |first=Steve |date=December 13, 2009 |work=[[TheWrap]] |access-date=December 13, 2009}} which was unprecedented at the time. Both films received numerous nominations in the awards' new craft categories, benefiting from the recent expansion of the categories. In the following years, this record has been broken several times. ''[[Avatar (2009 film)|Avatar]]'' followed close behind with nine nominations and won the most awards of the night with a then-record-breaking six wins. ==Winners and nominees== [[File:Kathryn Bigelow
